```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)

# Load the three files exactly as provided (no edits to the original CSVs)
GSE.covar.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_covar-1.csv")

GSE.GE.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")

GSE.GN.raw <-read_csv("~/Desktop/HDS/HSE103/FinalProject/GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```


## Step 1: Clean the covariate data

```{r}

head(GSE.covar.raw)
summary(GSE.covar.raw)

# Data Wrangling time! Whoohoo! Seems like there are some extra text in some
# columns that make unwanted 'noise'. With the help of the trusty mutate function
# we can clean these cells up!
GSE.covar <- GSE.covar.raw %>%
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = str_remove_all(mat_age_yrs,"age_years: "),
    preg_preeclampsia = str_remove_all(preg_preeclampsia, "pregnancy_condition: "),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = str_remove_all(delivery_gestAge_wks, "gestation_weeks: "),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = str_remove_all(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks, "blood_draw_at_gestation_week: "),
    batch_Microarray = str_remove_all(batch_Microarray, "microarray_hybridization_date: "),
    mat_BMI = str_remove_all(mat_BMI, "bmi_kg/m2: "),
    mat_vitD = str_remove_all(mat_vitD, "vitamind_25\\(0h\\)_ng/ml_whole_blood_baseline: "),
    mat_asthma = ifelse(str_ends(mat_asthma, "1"), "1", "0"))


# I also noticed all varaibles are stored as characters, for safe keeping
# I am going to change the ones that look like numeric measure to numeric 
GSE.covar <- GSE.covar %>%
  mutate(across(c(mat_age_yrs, delivery_gestAge_wks, sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                  mat_BMI, mat_vitD),
                as.numeric))


head(GSE.covar)
dim(GSE.covar)
```


## Step 2: Make the categorical variables

```{r}
# Categorical variable #1: preeclampsia status (already categories, so we just
# tell R it's a factor and put "Normal" first so it is the reference group).
# Categorical variable #2: vitamin D status, DERIVED from the continuous
# mat_vitD column. Under 20 ng/mL is a commonly used cutoff for deficiency.

GSE.covar <- GSE.covar %>%
  mutate(
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia,
                               levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
    vitD_status = factor(ifelse(mat_vitD < 20,
                                "Deficient (<20 ng/mL)",
                                "Sufficient (>=20 ng/mL)"),
                         levels = c("Deficient (<20 ng/mL)",
                                    "Sufficient (>=20 ng/mL)")))


# Check that the new variable makes sense: group sizes, and that the cutoff
# really split the vitamin D values where we said it would.
table(GSE.covar$preg_preeclampsia, GSE.covar$vitD_status)
GSE.covar %>% group_by(vitD_status) %>% summarise(min = min(mat_vitD), max = max(mat_vitD))

```

## Step 3: Clean the gene expression data and attach gene names

```{r}
# The first column of the expression file has a blank header, so we name it
# PROBEID. Probe IDs are just labels, so we store them as text in both tables
# so that R can match them up.

GSE.GE <- GSE.GE.raw %>%
  rename(PROBEID = 1) %>%
  mutate(PROBEID = as.character(PROBEID))

GSE.GN <- GSE.GN.raw %>%
  mutate(PROBEID = as.character(PROBEID))

# Step A: look up the gene name for each probe 
# Step B: pivot_longer turns the sideways table (one column per person) into a
#         tall table with one row per gene per person.

GSE.GE <- GSE.GE %>%
  left_join(GSE.GN, by = "PROBEID") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(PROBEID, GENE),
               names_to = "geoID",
               values_to = "expression")

# Safety checks: every probe got a gene name, and the sample IDs in the
# expression data are exactly the sample IDs in the covariate data.
stopifnot(!any(is.na(GSE.GE$GENE)))
stopifnot(setequal(unique(GSE.GE$geoID), GSE.covar$geoID))

head(GSE.GE)
```

## Step 4: Pick our gene and build the plotting table

```{r}
# Not every gene in the linker file is in the expression data, so check first!
gene_of_interest <- "RUNDC3A"
gene_of_interest %in% GSE.GE$GENE   # should be TRUE

# Keep just our gene, then attach each person's covariates using geoID
dat <- GSE.GE %>%
  filter(GENE == gene_of_interest) %>%
  left_join(GSE.covar, by = "geoID")

# Should be 157 rows: one per person
stopifnot(nrow(dat) == nrow(GSE.covar))
head(dat)
```

## Plot 1: Histogram of gene expression

```{r}
# Plot 1: Histogram of gene expression

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation of expression across all 157 people
# so we can put them on the plot.
m <- mean(dat$expression); s <- sd(dat$expression)


# Each bar counts how many people fall in that expression range.
# The dashed orange line marks the mean, and the text box in the top right
# corner gives the sample size, mean, and SD (\n starts a new line).
ggplot(dat, aes(x = expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#0072B2", color = "white") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = m, color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 5,
           label = sprintf("n = %d\nMean = %.2f\nSD = %.2f", nrow(dat), m, s)) +
  labs(x = paste(gene_of_interest, "expression level"),
       y = "Number of samples") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

## Plot 2: Scatterplot of covariate vs. gene expression

```{r}
# Plot 2: Scatterplot of covariate vs. gene expression

# Pearson correlation test between BMI and expression. We save it as "ct" so we
# can pull out r (strength/direction of the relationship) and the p-value.
ct <- cor.test(dat$mat_BMI, dat$expression)

# Each dot is one person. The line is a straight-line fit with its
# 95% confidence band, to show the overall trend.
ggplot(dat, aes(x = mat_BMI, y = expression)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "#0072B2") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "#D55E00",
              fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.2) +
  # Text box in the top left corner (-Inf, Inf) showing r, the p-value, and how
  # many people have a BMI value. sum(!is.na(...)) counts the non-missing BMIs.
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 5,
           label = sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.2f\nn = %d", ct$estimate, ct$p.value, sum(!is.na(dat$mat_BMI)))) +
  labs(x = expression("Maternal BMI (kg/m"^2*")"),
       y = paste(gene_of_interest, "expression level")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

## Plot 3: Boxplot of gene expression by both categorical variables

```{r}
# Plot 3: Boxplot of gene expression by both categorical variables

# Linear model: does expression differ by preeclampsia and/or vitamin D status?
# Each effect is estimated while holding the other one fixed.
fit <- lm(expression ~ preg_preeclampsia + vitD_status, data = dat)
# Pull out the table of estimates, standard errors, t values, and p-values
coef <- summary(fit)$coefficients

# x-axis = preeclampsia status, colour = vitamin D status.
# Dots show the individual samples so readers can see the group sizes.
ggplot(dat, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = expression, fill = vitD_status)) +
# Boxes show the median and spread. outlier.shape = NA hides the default
# outlier dots since we draw every dot ourselves below.
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
# Individual people as dots, jittered sideways so they don't stack on top 
# of each other, and lined up over the correct box. show.legend = FALSE 
# keeps them out of the legend.
   geom_point(aes(group = vitD_status),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                             dodge.width = 0.8),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
# Print the group size (n = ...) above each box at height y = 11.4.
# length(y) counts how many people are in that group.
  stat_summary(fun.data = function(y) data.frame(y = 11.4, label = paste0("n = ", length(y))),
               geom = "text", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")) +
  labs(x = "Pregnancy outcome",
       y = paste(gene_of_interest, "expression level"),
       fill = "Vitamin D status") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
```
